Kai (Customer): Hey team — starting ~30m ago our Dedicated cluster for org-orion started seeing sustained TPS spikes (~600 req/s) and we're getting a lot of 429s + some 503s. Burst credits show at 0 in console. Can you help?
Maya S.: Sorry you're seeing that — looking now. Which cluster/region and model variant are you hitting? Any request ids you can paste?
Kai (Customer): cluster: orion-prod-us-west, model: rw-14b-v2-fp16, region us-west-2. A couple request ids: req_20260317_01, req_20260317_02. We saw latency jump >1.2s per token and then the admission control started rejecting. Logs show admission_reject_reason=burst_credit_exhausted.
Liam R.: Thanks. Quick checks: can you confirm traffic pattern (single client fanout vs many clients)? Also whether this is sustained or spiky bursts?
Kai (Customer): It's a combination — an automated campaign kicked off by a partner and then a steady background from webhooks. It ramped up fast, so autoscaler may not have enough headroom.
Anika P.: Copy. I'm pulling the admission control trace and quota state. Maya — opening a temporary escalation.
Maya S.: autoscale-bot, can you show the recent autoscaler decisions for orion-prod-us-west for the last 40m?
autoscale-bot: Pulling policy decisions from 1941999000 -> 1942001120 for cluster orion-prod-us-west...
autoscale-bot: Recent events: [timestamp=1941999805] scale_up_started -> +1 pod; [timestamp=1942000201] scale_up_delay due to safety_window=120s; [timestamp=1942000450] admission_headroom_low triggered; [timestamp=1942000980] burst_credit_transition -> 0.
Liam R.: Looks like safety_window throttled aggressive scaling; only one extra pod came up while TPS kept climbing. That, plus immediate burst credit exhaustion, explains the 429s.
Maya S.: Kai — two immediate mitigations: 1) we can apply a temporary admission headroom override for your cluster to give +20% token headroom for 15 minutes, 2) we can provision a short-term reserved burst credit top-up (emergency) while we review autoscaler config. Which would you prefer?
Kai (Customer): Please do both if possible. We need to bring failed requests down immediately.
Anika P.: Kicking off headroom override and requesting credit top-up. Also working with SRE to relax safety_window for the next 10 minutes.
Liam R.: Notes for postmortem — autoscaler config snippet from this cluster: ```yaml
autoscaler:
  min_pods: 2
  max_pods: 10
  scale_up_cooldown: 120s
  scale_down_cooldown: 180s
  policy: cpu_token_hybrid
  emergency_headroom_percent: 10
```
Liam R.: Proposed changes to avoid similar rejections: reduce scale_up_cooldown to 30s for burst-prone customers, increase emergency_headroom_percent to 25% for orgs with webhook-driven traffic, and add a predictive ramp detector.
Maya S.: For reproducibility, can you provide a minimal repro script that caused the spike? Kai provided a sample: ```bash
for i in {1..700}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" \
    -d '{"model":"rw-14b-v2-fp16","input":"test ${i}"}' &
done
wait
```
Maya S.: We ran the repro in a staging cluster and reproduced admission_reject_reason=burst_credit_exhausted after ~420 req/s sustained. In staging we have autoscaler with a shorter cooldown so it recovered with scaling; in prod the safety_window prevents enough pods from starting fast enough.
Anika P.: Sent emergency credit top-up +20k tokens and applied headroom override +25% for 30m. Logging note: watch for admission_control.observe events.
Kai (Customer): Thanks — now we see 429s dropping and latency normalizing. Appreciate the fast help.
Liam R.: After action items: 1) run a config change to reduce scale_up_cooldown for this customer class, 2) add a pre-warming rule to start an extra pod when short-term traffic forecast >400 TPS, 3) review burst credit allocation model and consider dynamic refill thresholds.
Maya S.: I'll open a ticket for the config changes and flag for product to discuss default safety_window and headroom values for Dedicated. Ticket: INC-20260317-ORION-01.
Anika P.: For the postmortem, please include these artifacts: K8s events for orion-prod-us-west 1941999400-1942001400, admission_control logs (filtered by req_20260317_*), autoscaler metrics (scale decisions, pod startup latency), and the customer repro script.
Kai (Customer): Will upload the repro script and some client logs to the ticket. Thanks again. :+1:
Maya S.: Closing loop for now. If you see a regression ping this thread and we'll reopen. :wave:
